_meta.primary_legislation: Body Corporate and Community Management Act 1997 (QLD)
_meta.trust_law: BCCM Act 1997; Standard Module Regulation; Accommodation Module Regulation

max_interest_rate_pa.legislation: BCCM Accommodation Module reg 157; Standard Module reg 100(7)
max_interest_rate_pa.notes: QLD interest ceiling is 2.5% per month (Accommodation Module reg 157), which equates to a maximum of 30% per annum simple interest.

max_interest_rate_pa_by_special_resoluti.notes: 2.5% per month is the statutory ceiling. Expressed as annual: 30%.

interest_grace_period_days.notes: No statutory grace period — interest accrues from the day the contribution falls due.

can_transfer_between_funds.legislation: BCCM Standard Module reg 100(7); Accommodation Module reg 157
can_transfer_between_funds.notes: Inter-fund transfers (e.g. admin→sinking) are PROHIBITED under the Standard Module and Accommodation Module.

inter_fund_transfer_resolution_required.notes: No resolution can authorise an inter-fund transfer in QLD — the prohibition is absolute. Allowed values: none, ordinary, general_meeting, special, prohibited.

overbudget_threshold_pct.notes: QLD does not impose a statutory over-budget percentage threshold.

overbudget_requires_resolution_above_pct.notes: No statutory over-budget resolution trigger in QLD.

trust_withdrawal_authority_roles.notes: Body corporate owns the bank account directly. Withdrawals authorised by committee resolution (majority) or by the body corporate manager per their contract.

trial_balance_deadline_days.notes: Monthly financial statement required — effectively a 30-day deadline after month-end.

audit_deadline.notes: Financial statements tabled at AGM; audit completed unless resolved otherwise.

pooled_trust_permitted.notes: Body corporate owns the bank account directly — there is no manager-held pooled trust arrangement.

interest_belongs_to.notes: The body corporate owns the account and receives all interest directly. Allowed values: scheme, statutory_account, body_corporate.

committee_spending_cap_formula.notes: Default committee spending cap: $200 per lot. Requires a committee resolution for amounts above this threshold. Total cap = $200 × number of lots in the scheme.

committee_spending_cap_per_lot_cents.notes: Per-lot committee spending cap in integer cents ($200 = 20000 cents).

min_withholding_pct_no_abn.notes: ATO PAYG withholding: 47% on payments to suppliers without ABN.

levy_interest_rate_default_percent.notes: Default monthly interest on unpaid contributions: 2.5% per month.

levy_interest_rate_min_percent.notes: Body corporate may resolve a lower rate.

audit_threshold_budget_aud.notes: QLD: all schemes above a minimum size must have accounts reviewed annually. Threshold set by regulation.

audit_threshold_lots.notes: All schemes required to have financial accounts reviewed/audited annually.

building_insurance_required.notes: Building insurance at replacement value — mandatory.

sinking_fund_review_years.notes: Sinking fund plan reviewed every 10 years.

record_inspection_days.notes: Records must be available for inspection within 14 days of request.

capital_funding_standard_notice_days.legislation: BCCM Act 1997 s.141; Queensland Government contribution notice guidance
capital_funding_standard_notice_days.notes: Owners must receive written contribution notices at least 30 days before the contribution falls due.

capital_funding_emergency_notice_days.notes: No shorter generic emergency levy period is encoded; urgent funding structures require legal-review override.

capital_funding_notice_period_verified.legislation: BCCM Act 1997 s.141; Queensland Government contribution notice guidance
capital_funding_notice_period_verified.notes: The 30-day written contribution notice period is encoded from Queensland Government guidance.

capital_funding_resolution_required.legislation: BCCM Act 1997; Queensland Government contribution guidance
capital_funding_resolution_required.notes: Special contributions are generally approved by ordinary resolution.

capital_funding_allocation_basis.notes: Contributions are calculated using contribution schedule lot entitlements unless a statutory exception applies.

capital_funding_benefit_principle_availa.notes: The default capital-funding allocator is the contribution schedule lot entitlement; mixed-use exceptions require legal review.

capital_funding_tenant_consultation_requ.notes: Tenant consultation is not a default contribution-approval condition; works access and by-law communications are separate workflows.

capital_funding_hardship_notice_required.notes: No QLD-specific hardship notice requirement is encoded; payment-plan controls can still be offered as product policy.

capital_funding_hybrid_legal_review_requ.notes: Hybrid owner-funded and loan-funded structures require recorded legal approval before notices or credits are issued.
